text:
sara: Quick sync — we want to change per-route quota precedence so route-level overrides account-level limits (route wins). Planning: add an explicit response header and a small SDK patch to surface route vs account quota hits. Can we confirm compatibility and a safe canary plan?
liam: Quick Q — how will this show up to clients on 429s? soft vs hard 429 semantics?
jorge: Proposal: add `X-RateLimit-Route` with format `limit:window_seconds` and keep `X-RateLimit-Account` for account-level. 429 body will include `{"exceeded":"route"}` when route blocked. Old clients will ignore unknown headers (backcompat).
anna: +1 on header shape. For soft-429s we should still return 200 with body indicating degraded result; this change only affects hard 429 (throttled).
sara: Correct — only hard 429s. Soft-degrade behavior remains unchanged. SDK change: expose header parsing and raise a specific `RouteQuotaError` (python/ts) with `limit` and `retry_after`.
jorge: Example header + body we plan to emit:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Route: 50:60
X-RateLimit-Account: 1000:60
Retry-After: 12
Content-Type: application/json

{"type":"quota_exceeded","level":"route","retry_after":12}
```
liam: Will the `Retry-After` remain authoritative for backoff? we need SDKs to honor it over heuristics.
anna: Yes, `Retry-After` wins. SDKs should expose both `retry_after` and `level` so app logic can do graceful fallbacks.
sara: Canary plan: roll header change + SDK patch together. Server: roll to 5% traffic in us-east first. SDKs: publish minor package with opt-in flag `respect_route_quota=true` so apps can opt into stricter handling immediately. Monitor 429 counts, percent of route-level vs account-level, and user-facing error spikes.
deploy-bot: Canary scheduled: server change -> 2024-08-14T18:00Z to 5% (us-east). SDKs will be published as 0.9.1-beta. :white_check_mark:
jorge: Test checklist I propose: unit parse tests for header, integration test simulating route-exceed, e2e with canary traffic generator (script + k6), and regression test ensuring older SDK versions ignore header (no 500s).
liam: Also add a smoke test that ensures fallback routing (route-blocked -> try lower-cap model variant) occurs within 100ms of 429 handling.
anna: Ops alerts: create temporary dashboard panels for `429_rate_by_level`, `route_429_ratio`, `sdk_retry_success_rate`. Add alert if user-facing error rate > 0.5% for the canary cohort.
sara: Sounds good. Action items: @jorge add header emit + tests PR, @liam add SDK opt-in patch, @anna create dashboards + alert, I'll schedule canary & monitor. Any objections?
liam: no objections. :+1:
jorge: Will put a short PR description that outlines backcompat: "unknown headers are ignored; behavior unchanged for old SDKs".
anna: Will create the dashboards and share links here when ready. :eyes:
sara: Thanks team — will follow up with the PR links and canary runbook.
